answer: Trust propagates from vetted seeds through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, with each step respecting edge weights and a fixed walk-length limit. A sybil cluster—whether its nodes are labeled sable, marble, or yarrow—has low conductance when few weighted edges cross its boundary relative to its volume. Such a sparse external cut limits how often walks from honest seeds enter the cluster, mathematically bounding its aggregate voting weight by its trusted connectivity rather than its number of identities.
